question: As of 10 August 2026, what cash price per share had the consortium of CPP Investments and ReNew Energy Global's founder-CEO Sumant Sinha put to ReNew's board, was that price legally binding at that date, what premium did it represent to ReNew's US$6.24 closing price on 28 May 2026, and by how much had it risen from the consortium's first proposal?
grading: Key points (all required): (1) price = US$7.02 per share in cash (with a rollover alternative for eligible shareholders); (2) status as of 10 August 2026 = 'best and final' NON-binding proposal dated 27 July 2026 (reaffirmed by confirmatory letter dated 6 August), not a definitive agreement; (3) premium = 12.5% to the US$6.24 close on 28 May 2026; (4) increase of US$0.27 (4.0%) from the first non-binding proposal of US$6.75 dated 28 May 2026. Accept 'about 12.5%' and 'about 4%'. Fail if the answer says a definitive/binding agreement existed on or before 10 August, uses US$6.75 as the current price, quotes the implied US$10.2bn EV or the Q1 2027 completion date as already announced, or uses a premium measured against a different reference price.
answer: US$7.02 in cash per ReNew share, in the consortium's 'best and final' non-binding proposal dated 27 July 2026 (announced 28 July) and reaffirmed by a confirmatory letter dated 6 August; the independent Special Committee was still evaluating it, so as of 10 August it was not binding (the definitive agreement was signed on 11 August). It is a 12.5% premium to the US$6.24 close on 28 May 2026 and US$0.27 (4.0%) above the consortium's first non-binding proposal of US$6.75 dated 28 May 2026 (announced 29 May) [W05-E1, W05-E2].

output.answer:
**As of 10 August 2026, the consortium's offer stood at US$7.02 per share — non-binding.**

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| **Price per share** | **US$7.02 in cash** |
| **Legally binding?** | **No** — it remained a "best and final **non-binding** proposal" |
| **Premium to US$6.24 (28 May 2026 close)** | **12.5%** |
| **Increase from first proposal** | **US$0.27 per share, or 4.0%** (up from US$6.75) |

**Context:**
- The consortium (CPP Investments + founder/Chairman/CEO Sumant Sinha) first proposed **US$6.75/share** in a non-binding letter dated 28 May 2026 (announced 29 May), an 8.2% premium to the $6.24 close.
- A "best and final" non-binding proposal of **US$7.02** followed on **27 July 2026** (announced 28 July).
- On **6 August 2026**, the consortium sent a confirmatory letter reaffirming the July 27 terms at US$7.02 as its best and final **non-binding** proposal — so as of 10 August it was still non-binding.
- The offer only became contractually binding when ReNew entered into the **Transaction Agreement dated 11 August 2026**. The cash offer was subsequently confirmed at US$7.02, a 12.5% premium to the $6.24 close and 24.7% to the one-month VWAP of $5.63, valuing ReNew at ~US$2.8bn equity / ~US$10.2bn enterprise value.

Sources:
- [SEC Form 6-K (confirmatory letter, 6 Aug 2026)](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/RNW/6-k-re-new-energy-global-plc-current-report-foreign-issuer-49100be9dd49.html)
- [SEC EX-99.2 / Project Surya transaction announcement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1848763/000119312526343552/d104914dex992.htm)
- [SEC Form 6-K (11 Aug 2026 Transaction Agreement)](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/RNW/6-k-re-new-energy-global-plc-current-report-foreign-issuer-22fa3b74486a.html)
- [SEC Form 6-K (28 May 2026 US$6.75 proposal)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1848763/000119312526246389/6k_cppib_may_29.htm)

Note the distinction: the $6.75 first proposal (28 May 2026) was an 8.2% premium to $6.24; the $7.02 best-and-final was 12.5% to the same reference price.
